title: Sandpaper George and other improvised instruments
summary: He recalls a fish-fry rhythm man who rubbed sandpaper, the bazooka-like instrument and a homemade tub-and-string bass.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well there used to be a group that used to make all these fish fries around that particular time. And one of the fellas I remember very well, he used to call him Sand Paper George. Oh I've heard of him. The thing about it, he used to give the group rhythm, you know, he had pieces of sandpaper, he used to rub them together and you'd be surprised at the type of rhythm you would get from it. And I had noticed him in several places, you know, even sometimes the local spots, you know, in the barrooms, and he'd go in there and he'd join with various groups. And every time there was a band of music on the corner he'd jump on the truck and pull out his sandpaper. So he was particularly musically, he just had that feeling. How old was he? Well he was much older than I was. At that particular time I would say he was around in his 30s, in his middle 30s, of course I was a little bit of a fella myself.
Maybe he's still around in the city. Maybe we can play.

Possibly so. You can never tell. But they had a very unique aggregation wherein he played the sandpaper and another fella played the kazoo and this instrument's built like a bazooka. Of course I don't know where the idea was taken from that instrument, wherein George Burns used to play the bazooka. It could have been.
He probably had those in New Orleans first I think.
Yes. And then too they had another type of instrument which one of the fellas had developed himself. It was made out of a wash tub with a pole running perpendicular from the base of the tub.
Wherein it had strings and he could key those strings down and get almost any note you wanted to. And the change was not too far, but in all he got the desired results he wanted to get.
